title: Reading Drill — Testing a shallow pond ramp — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Testing a shallow pond ramp — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Millcross, work on animals reaching the edge but being unable to leave the water had already produced a small collection of daytime observations. The wildlife centre staff used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: successful exits.

**B** The group kept a rougher ramp surface for the new trial, which was planned to run for three weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that fluctuating water height should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
